Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 10, verse 103:

﴿Then We shall save Our messengers and those who believed. Thus it is due upon Us: We shall save the believers.﴾: When His saying ﴿Then do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ [Yunus: 102] had preceded, and that implied what had befallen the earlier nations who denied, and explicitly stated their destruction in more than one verse, He, exalted is He, related the account of their past condition, saying: ﴿Then We shall save Our messengers﴾. The meaning is: those who passed away, We destroyed them when they denied the messengers, then We saved the messengers and the believers. For this reason al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿Then We shall save﴾ is conjoined to an omitted statement indicated by ﴿but the like of the days of those who passed away before them﴾ [Yunus: 102], as if it were said: We destroy the nations, then We save Our messengers, in accordance with the past accounts.

The apparent view is that ﴿thus﴾ is in the accusative position, its implied sense being: like that salvation by which We saved the messengers and their believers, We save whoever believes in you, O Muhammad. And ﴿due﴾ is in the sense of: that is due as a due obligation.

Abu al-Baqa said: it is permissible for ﴿due﴾ to be a substitute (badal) for the omitted element that the particle "ka" (thus) stands in for, its implied sense being: the salvation of the like of that is due. He also permitted both ﴿thus﴾ and ﴿due﴾ to be in the accusative governed by the following ﴿We shall save﴾, and that ﴿thus﴾ be accusative governed by the first ﴿We shall save﴾, and ﴿due﴾ by the second ﴿We shall save﴾. He also permitted, following Ibn Atiyya, that the particle "ka" be in the nominative position, its implied sense being: the matter is thus, and ﴿due﴾ is accusative governed by what follows it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿like that salvation, We save the believers among you and destroy the polytheists﴾, and ﴿due upon Us﴾ is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad), meaning: that is due upon Us as a due obligation. Al-Qadi said: what is meant by ﴿due upon Us﴾ is obligation, because the deliverance of the Messenger ﷺ and the believers from punishment to reward is obligatory, and were it not so, it would not be good of God to impose upon them arduous acts.

When this is established for this reason, it takes the place of the discharge of a debt for a preceding cause. It was answered that it is due according to promise and decree, not according to entitlement, since it is established that a servant has no claim against his Creator for anything.

Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ﴿nunjī al-mu'minīn﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88] with lightening, the present tense of anja (to save). The orthography of the Mushaf is nunj without a yā'.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 10, verses 104–107:

﴿Say: "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die. And I have been commanded to be among the believers."﴾ ﴿And [I was commanded], "Direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be among the polytheists."﴾ ﴿And do not invoke besides Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you. For if you did, then you would be, at that time, among the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He wills good for you, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾: It is an address to the people of Makkah, saying: If you do not know what I am upon, then I will explain it to you. So he began first by disavowing the worship of what they worship of idols, deriding their opinions, and then he affirmed second who it is that he worships, namely Allah, "who causes you to die."

In mentioning this attribute, the middle one that indicates causing death, there is an indication of the beginning, which is creation, and of the return. It is as if he pointed out that he worships Allah, who created you, causes you to die, and will restore you. The three stages are mentioned explicitly many times in the Qur'an. The explicit mention of this attribute serves as a reminder of death, a means of striking fear into souls, and of their return to Allah after it. He is the one worthy of being feared, guarded against, and worshipped, not the stones you worship.

﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾: When he mentioned that he worships Allah, and worship is mostly done through the actions of the limbs, he informed them that he was commanded to be among those who affirm Allah and profess His oneness, those who single Him out in worship, and he moved from the actions of the limbs to the light of knowledge, so that the inward matched the outward. Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that Allah the Exalted commanded me by what He placed in me of intellect, and by what He revealed to me in His Book.

It has also been said that its meaning is: If you are in doubt about my religion and about what I am upon, whether I should remain steadfast or abandon it and agree with you, then do not entertain impossible thoughts, do not doubt my affair, cut off your hopes regarding me, and know that I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, nor do I choose misguidance over guidance, as in His saying: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1] ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 2]. ﴿And I have been commanded to be﴾ [Yunus: 72]: its origin is "bi-an akuna" (that I be), so the preposition was omitted. This omission may be of the regular kind, which is the omission of prepositions with "an" and "anna," and it may be of the irregular kind, as in his saying: "amartuka al-khayr" (I commanded you the good), ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾ [al-Hijr: 94]. End.

He means by the irregular omission his saying "amartuka al-khayr": that the preposition is not omitted from the second object except in a limited set of verbs by transmission, not by analogy. These are: ikhtara (chose), istaghfara (sought forgiveness), amara (commanded), sammā (named), labbā (responded), and da'a in the sense of sammā (named), zawwaja (married), and saddaqa (confirmed), contrary to those who take the omission of the preposition from the second object as analogical, where they mean the preposition itself, and the place of omission is like: "baraytu al-qalam bi-al-sikkin" (I sharpened the pen with the knife), so they permit "al-sikkin" in the accusative.

The answer to "in kuntum fi shakk" (if you are in doubt) is his saying "fa-la a'budu" (then I do not worship), and the estimate is "fa-ana la a'budu" (then I do not worship), because the negated verb with "la," when it occurs as an answer, is jussive; when the "fa" enters upon it, it is known that it is by the implied subject. The same applies if "duna" is not with "la" in his saying:

﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95], meaning: "fa-huwa yantaqimu Allahu minhu" (then He, Allah, takes retribution from him). His saying "fa-la a'budu" implicitly contains the meaning: "fa-ana mukhalifukum" (then I oppose you).

﴿And [I was commanded] that I establish﴾: It may be that it is governed by his saying "wa-ummirtu" (and I was commanded), with regard to meaning, because the meaning of his saying "an akuna" (that I be) is: "Be among the believers," so "an" is a verbal (masdariyyah) particle whose clause is the imperative. The grammarians have permitted this, and they did not impose on its clause what is imposed on the clauses of relative pronouns, that they must be declarative under the conditions mentioned in grammar. It may also be that it is with an implied verb, i.e., "wa-uhiya ilayya an aqim" (and it was revealed to me that I establish). So it is possible that it is a verbal "an," and it is possible that it is an explanatory particle, because the implied clause carries the sense of saying. Positing an implied verb is preferable, to remove the awkwardness of coordination given the presence of the kaf, for if "wa-an aqim" were coordinated with "an akuna," the construction would be "wajhi" with the first-person ya', and taking the meaning into account there would be weak, while positing a verb is more common than observing coordination with respect to meaning. The "wajh" here means the direction and the aim, i.e., "istaqim li-al-din" (be upright in the religion) and do not swerve from it, and by this he figuratively refers to directing the intellect entirely to seeking the religion. "Hanifan" (inclining) is a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in "aqim," or from the object. Al-Zamakhshari permitted that it be a circumstantial accusative from "al-din" (religion).

"Wa-la tad'u" (and do not invoke): it may be a new prohibition, and it may be coordinated with "aqim," in which case it falls within the scope of "an" in both its forms, as a verbal particle and as an explanatory particle.

If the invocation of idols is forbidden, then their worship is all the more deserving of prohibition. ﴿fa-in fa'alta﴾ (And if you did): he used the verb to refer to invocation, for brevity, meaning: "fa-in da'awta ma la yanfa'uka wa-la yadurruka" (if you invoked what neither benefits nor harms you). The answer to the condition is "fa-innaka" and its predicate, and "idhan" was placed between the subject of "inna" and its predicate, though its rank is after the predicate, but the rhyme was observed in this. Al-Hawfi said: "al-fa'" is the answer to the condition, and "idhan" is an intermediate particle with no governing function; what is intended by it here is: "idha kana dhalik" (if that is the case). This is an explanation of the meaning, and it does not fit the sense of an answer. End.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "idhan" is the answer to the condition, and it is an answer to an implied question, as if a questioner asked about the consequence of worshipping idols. He was made among the wrongdoers because there is no wrong greater than polytheism: ﴿Indeed, association with Allah is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. End.

His discussion of "idhan" requires reflection, and we have already presented our discussion of it at length in Surat al-Baqarah. When the prohibition against invoking idols was issued, while they neither harm nor benefit, he mentioned that power, strength, benefit, and harm belong to none but Allah, and that He, the Exalted, is the One who alone possesses these. In "harm" he used the word "touch" (mass), and in "good" he used the word "will" (irada). He made a semantic antithesis between harm and good, not a verbal one, because the opposite of harm is benefit, and the opposite of good is evil. So the word "harm" came out more delicate and more specific than the word "evil," and the word "good" came out more complete than the word "benefit." The word "touch" is more concise than the word "will," and more explicit about reaching, and more fitting for His saying: ﴿there is no remover of it except Him﴾. The word "will" is more indicative of attainment at the time of address and at other times, and more fitting for the word "good," although "touch" and "will" both mean reaching. The response to ﴿And if Allah should touch you﴾ came with a general negation and an affirmation, and the response to ﴿And if He wills you﴾ came with a general negation, because what He wills cannot be repelled by any repeller, neither He nor other than Him, since His will is eternal and does not change; therefore the construction did not come as "fa-la radda lahu illa huwa."

"Touch," as an act, is an attribute of an action that brings about and lifts it, unlike "will," which is an attribute of the essence. And ﴿fa-la radda li-fadlihi﴾ (there is no repeller of His bounty): he named the good "bounty," indicating that the goods (p-197) from Allah the Exalted are issued by way of bounty, kindness, and favor. Then he expanded in reporting about the bounty and the good, saying: ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾. Then he informed of the two attributes indicating non-punishment, namely: the Forgiving, who conceals and pardons sins, and the Merciful, whose mercy precedes His wrath.

Since his saying ﴿and do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you﴾ had preceded, and he delayed the harm, it was fitting that the beginning be with the conditional clause related to harm. Also, since the disbelievers were expected to cause harm to the believers, while benefit was not hoped for from them, the precedence of the clause of harm was more emphatic in the report, so it was begun with.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): why did he mention "touch" in one and "will" in the second? I say: it is as if he intended to mention both matters together: the will and the reaching in each of harm and good, and that there is no repeller of what He wills of them, nor remover of what He reaches with them. So he was concise in speech: by mentioning "touch," which is reaching, in one, and "will," which is accomplishment, in the other, so that what he mentioned indicates what he omitted, that He has indeed repeated the reaching in good in His saying: "He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants." The meaning of "will" here is: the interest (maslaha). End.

It is as if he pointed out that he worships Allah, who created you, causes you to die, and will restore you. The three stages are mentioned explicitly many times in the Qur'an. The explicit mention of this attribute serves as a reminder of death, a means of striking fear into souls, and of their return to Allah after it. He is the one worthy of being feared, guarded against, and worshipped, not the stones you worship.

﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾: When he mentioned that he worships Allah, and worship is mostly done through the actions of the limbs, he informed them that he was commanded to be among those who affirm Allah and profess His oneness, those who single Him out in worship, and he moved from the actions of the limbs to the light of knowledge, so that the inward matched the outward. Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that Allah the Exalted commanded me by what He placed in me of intellect, and by what He revealed to me in His Book.

It has also been said that its meaning is: If you are in doubt about my religion and about what I am upon, whether I should remain steadfast or abandon it and agree with you, then do not entertain impossible thoughts, do not doubt my affair, cut off your hopes regarding me, and know that I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, nor do I choose misguidance over guidance, as in His saying: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1] ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 2]. ﴿And I have been commanded to be﴾ [Yunus: 72]: its origin is "bi-an akuna" (that I be), so the preposition was omitted. This omission may be of the regular kind, which is the omission of prepositions with "an" and "anna," and it may be of the irregular kind, as in his saying: "amartuka al-khayr" (I commanded you the good), ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾ [al-Hijr: 94]. End.

He means by the irregular omission his saying "amartuka al-khayr": that the preposition is not omitted from the second object except in a limited set of verbs by transmission, not by analogy. These are: ikhtara (chose), istaghfara (sought forgiveness), amara (commanded), sammā (named), labbā (responded), and da'a in the sense of sammā (named), zawwaja (married), and saddaqa (confirmed), contrary to those who take the omission of the preposition from the second object as analogical, where they mean the preposition itself, and the place of omission is like: "baraytu al-qalam bi-al-sikkin" (I sharpened the pen with the knife), so they permit "al-sikkin" in the accusative.

The answer to "in kuntum fi shakk" (if you are in doubt) is his saying "fa-la a'budu" (then I do not worship), and the estimate is "fa-ana la a'budu" (then I do not worship), because the negated verb with "la," when it occurs as an answer, is jussive; when the "fa" enters upon it, it is known that it is by the implied subject. The same applies if "duna" is not with "la" in his saying:

﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95], meaning: "fa-huwa yantaqimu Allahu minhu" (then He, Allah, takes retribution from him). His saying "fa-la a'budu" implicitly contains the meaning: "fa-ana mukhalifukum" (then I oppose you).

The grammarians have permitted this, and they did not impose on its clause what is imposed on the clauses of relative pronouns, that they must be declarative under the conditions mentioned in grammar. It may also be that it is with an implied verb, i.e., "wa-uhiya ilayya an aqim" (and it was revealed to me that I establish). Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 10, verses 108–109:

﴿Say, "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided, it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is guided; and whoever goes astray, it is only against it that he goes astray. And I am not over you a manager."﴾ ﴿And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges. And He is the best of judges.﴾ Al-Haqq (the truth): the Qur'an, or the Messenger, or the religion of Islam — three opinions. The meaning: the reward of his guidance is attained by him, and the burden of his misguidance falls upon him. Guidance and misguidance occur by the will of Allah the Exalted from the servant; this is the position of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah, the adherents of the prophetic tradition).

And whoever has been decreed guidance in eternity will surely attain it, and whoever has been decreed misguidance is likewise, and there is no escape from that.

Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: He, the Exalted, has made clear that He has perfected the Sharia, removed the pretext, and cut off the excuse: ﴿So whoever is guided, it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is guided; and whoever goes astray, it is only against it that he goes astray. And I am not over you a manager.﴾ Therefore it is not incumbent upon me to strive more in bringing you to the great reward and in rescuing you from the painful punishment than I have done. Al-Zamakhshari said: No excuse remains for you, and Allah the Exalted has no proof against you. Whoever chooses guidance and following the truth benefits only himself by his choice, and whoever prefers misguidance harms only himself.

The lam and ʿalā (in the phrase "li-nafsihi" and "ʿalayhā"): ʿalā here carries the sense of harm and the lam the sense of benefit. He entrusted the matter to them after removing the causes and making the truth manifest. In this there is an urging to adopt guidance and abandon misguidance in spite of that. ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾: a guardian to whom your affair is entrusted, or one who compels you to what I desire. I am only a bearer of good news and a warner, ended.

His words are an appendix to the words of al-Qadi, and it runs according to the school of the Mu'tazilah. His command, Exalted is He, to His Prophet to follow what is revealed to him is a command to persistence and to patience over what reaches you for the sake of Allah of the harm and turning away of the disbelievers. He qualified the command to be patient with His saying: ﴿until Allah judges﴾, and this is a promise from Him, the Exalted, of raising His word and granting victory over His enemies, as it occurred. Ibn ʿAbbas and a group went to the view that His saying: ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾ (and be patient) is abrogated by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf). And a group went to the view that it is muhkam (not abrogated), and they interpreted ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾ as meaning that he is not a watcher over their deeds so as to requite them for them; rather that belongs to Allah. And His saying "wa-isbir" (and be patient): [means] patience upon obedience to Allah, bearing the burdens of prophethood, and discharging the message. On this view there is no contradiction between these two verses and the verse of the sword, and to this the verifying scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) inclined. It is narrated that when "wa-isbir" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered the Ansar and said: "You will find after me favoritism, so be patient until you meet me." Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that I was commanded in this verse to be patient over what the disbelievers inflicted upon me, so I was patient; and you, be patient over what the oppressive rulers inflict upon you. Anas said: "So we did not show patience." Then he mentioned an account that took place between Abu Qatadah and Muawiyah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, which is to be consulted in his book.

His command, Exalted is He, to His Prophet to follow what is revealed to him is a command to persistence and to patience over what reaches you for the sake of Allah of the harm and turning away of the disbelievers. He qualified the command to be patient with His saying: ﴿until Allah judges﴾, and this is a promise from Him, the Exalted, of raising His word and granting victory over His enemies, as it occurred. Ibn ʿAbbas and a group went to the view that His saying: ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾ (and be patient) is abrogated by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf). And a group went to the view that it is muhkam (not abrogated), and they interpreted ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾ as meaning that he is not a watcher over their deeds so as to requite them for them; rather that belongs to Allah. And His saying "wa-isbir" (and be patient): [means] patience upon obedience to Allah, bearing the burdens of prophethood, and discharging the message. On this view there is no contradiction between these two verses and the verse of the sword, and to this the verifying scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) inclined. It is narrated that when "wa-isbir" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered the Ansar and said: "You will find after me favoritism, so be patient until you meet me." Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that I was commanded in this verse to be patient over what the disbelievers inflicted upon me, so I was patient; and you, be patient over what the oppressive rulers inflict upon you. Anas said: "So we did not show patience." Then he mentioned an account that took place between Abu Qatadah and Muawiyah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, which is to be consulted in his book.
